rationale: The plan correctly refuses de-duplication with the right reason (no UMIs, duplication tracks expression in deep total-RNA libraries) and keeps sample_01 unless it is a multivariate outlier, which matches the reference policy, and the DESeq2 Wald / edgeR QL, ~condition with control releveled, >=10 counts in >=6 samples filter, internal size factors, BH at 0.05 with apeglm are all explicit and appropriate for 6v6 unpaired single-batch data. The main gap is library-type specificity: it never reports rRNA fraction, mitochondrial fraction, or intronic share to actually explain the >60% duplication, and never considers whether high or uneven rRNA/MT content should be removed from the matrix before normalization — so the total-RNA aspect is acknowledged rhetorically but not operationalized in QC or in the size-factor step. Enrichment is well specified (Wald-stat ranking, named collections with versions, 15-500 size window, collapsePathways, leading edge, no pre-thresholding), though it goes beyond what the question asked. Reporting is thorough on versions, design, contrast, thresholds, tested/significant counts, and caveats.
